html:
The Jaega were a small Native people of the Atlantic coast of southeast Florida, around Jupiter Inlet and Lake Worth. They lived on fish, shellfish and wild plants and did not farm.

They were probably subject to the powerful Calusa of the southwest coast, and lived between the Tequesta to the south and the Ais to the north. In 1696 the Quaker merchant Jonathan Dickinson was shipwrecked on their coast; his journal describes the town of Hobe and its chief, and is one of the few records of them. Disease and slave raids from Carolina in the early 1700s destroyed them, and survivors may have left for Cuba with the Spanish of Spanish Florida.
